newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Pol Pot said under assault, ex-comrades block surrender.
newsitem.headline: Pol Pot said under assault, ex-comrades block surrender.

text.p: Former comrades-in-arms of hated Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot were making a final assault to capture him on Friday after refusing his offer to surrender, Cambodia's first prime minister said.
"They finally know where he is and will make a final assault today in the hope we will be able to capture Pol Pot alive," Prince Norodom Ranariddh told reporters.
Ranariddh said Pol Pot was holed up with 15 people but he would not identify them nor their location.
"I have heard clearly this morning that Pol Pot offered to surrender but the forces around him don't want him to surrender," he said.
Ranariddh was speaking at Ang Snuol, 20 km (12 miles) southwest of Phnom Penh at the opening of a religious meeting hall.

Asked why the forces opposing Pol Pot would not accept his surrender, Ranariddh said: "There is a great difference between surrender and capture. Surrender means we have to give Pol Pot safe conduct. We have to capture him alive."
Ranariddh called for Pol Pot to be placed on trial for the death of more than one million Cambodians during his "killing fields" rule of Cambodia from 1975 to 1979.
"As I have said many time before, send him to an international tribunal"

He said recent Khmer Rouge radio broadcasts, from a self-styled Provisional Government of National Solidarity, had come from the Anlong Veng camp in northern Cambodia where Pol Pot had been based but which was now in the hands of his foes.

Pol Pot fled north from Anlong Veng earlier this month after executing his defence chief and family members. Other members of the Khmer Rouge at Anlong Veng pursued Pol Pot and a group of loyalists who fled with him. Ranariddh said any suggestion that Khmer Rouge dissidents could establish a provisonal government was unacceptable.
"They can't have a provisonal government. It is not acceptable," he said.
"They have to recognise only one king, one head of state, one government."
